the maximum power of a gas bearing supported centrifugal compressor for a vapor compression cycle is limited by the compressor bearing load capacity and can be expressed as: Pmax = 0.1 × (ρev − ρcon) × (NDm)3.2 × (1.2 + 0.5 × Δf), where ρev is the evaporator pressure, ρcon is the condenser pressure, NDm

the maximum feasible power of gas bearing supported centrifugal compressors driving vapor compression cycles is limited by bearing load capacity, rotordynamic eigenfrequency and specific compressor speed and that this power is maximized by a family of refrigerants with critical temperatures between 150 K and 250 K and that the maximum power is expressed as a function only of the reduced evaopration pressure.

gas bearing supported turbomachinery is limited by the load capacity of the bearings and by the stability of the rotors and that there is a family (or range) of fluids for which the maximum feasible compressor powers are optimized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel concept of gas bearing supported centrifugal compressors that could enable a significant improvement in the performance of vapor compression cycles.

a novel, gas bearing supported centrifugal compressor design for driving vapor compression refrigeration cycles, and with a detailed thermodynamic analysis of the refrigerant selection for this application.
the development of a new generation of compact, low-power turbocompressors supported on gas bearings for driving vapor-compression cycles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the maximum compressor speed is a limiting factor for the power of gas bearing supported centrifugal compressors.

the maximum feasible power of gas bearing supported single-stage centrifugal turbocompressors is limited to the range from 50 kW to about 250 kWh, depending on the choice of the working fluid and on the compressor design.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the feasibility of gas bearing supported centrifugal compressors in vapor compression systems depends on the working fluid, the evaporator temperature, the condenser temperature and the bearing design.
the feasible maximum power is limited by bearing load capacity, rotordynamic stability margin, specific compressor speed, and bearing tip speed.

the maximum feasible power of a gas bearing supported turbomachine depends on the working fluid, the temperature lift between condenser and evaporator, the specific compressor speed and the bearing tip speed and the rotordynamic stability margin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the maximum feasible power of gas bearing supported compressors is limited, primarily, by the bearing load-carrying capacity.
the power range of vapor compression cycles is limited by the compressor bearing load capacity.
the maximum feasible power is a function of the working fluid selection, the compressor speed and the rotordynamic stability.
